clue.text: Virtually on level pegging

definitions.meaning: equal, matching in standard or score

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both 'nearly' (it is as good as finished) and 'equal to' (one is as good as another), matching each half.

clue.text: Slut accepts last rent review

indicators.note: a review looks over something again and reworks it, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A slovenly tenant takes a look at the latest rent increase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepts' is only a link here, joining definition to wordplay, though it reads as if the slut accepts something.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned insult for a dirty, untidy woman; both words name the same slovenly figure.

clue.text: Not a private place to dine

definitions.text: Not a private place to dine

parts.words: Not a private place to dine
parts.note: reads as a public restaurant, but 'private' is the army rank: the dining room is reserved for commissioned ranks, not ordinary soldiers

explanation.walkthrough: 'private' looks like the opposite of public; it is the lowest army rank, who may not eat in this room.
explanation.definitionFit: The military dining room reserved for commissioned ranks, which privates may not enter.

clue.text: Activist takes two seconds to find vagrant

indicators.note: the activist takes something into himself, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a doer is an active person who gets things done
S is the abbreviation for second, and two of them give a pair

explanation.surface: A campaigner takes a moment to locate a homeless person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes' is the container signal. A DOSSER is British slang for a rough sleeper, someone who dosses down anywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a homeless person sleeping rough, a tramp or drifter.

clue.text: Hurries back prior to revolution

indicators.note: back says the word for hurries is read in the backwards direction

parts.note: nips, as in nips out to the shop, means hurries

explanation.surface: Someone rushes home before an uprising breaks out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns NIPS around. 'revolution' suggests a political uprising but means a turn or rotation.
explanation.definitionFit: A single rotation or turn about an axis, as a wheel or dancer makes.

clue.text: Drive out from a woman's home

parts.note: Di is a common woman's name, and the possessive adds S
a lodge is a small house or dwelling

explanation.surface: Someone sets off on a car journey from a lady's house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drive out' reads like setting off in a car; it means to force out of position.
explanation.definitionFit: To force something or someone out of a fixed place, as from a position or hold.

clue.text: Identical notes sung by operatic heroine

indicators.note: identical notes means the same note sung twice over

parts.note: mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A soprano heroine sings the same notes again.
explanation.walkthrough: MIMI is the heroine of Puccini's La Bohème.
explanation.definitionFit: The consumptive seamstress who is the leading female role in Puccini's opera La Bohème.

clue.text: If you hear it, you'll wake up

definitions.text: If you hear it, you'll wake up

parts.words: If you hear it, you'll wake up
parts.note: describes a morning call, the bugle signal sounded to rouse soldiers from sleep

explanation.definitionFit: The bugle call played at dawn in army camps to rouse troops from bed.

clue.text: Former priest in disarray

indicators.note: in disarray means jumbled and out of order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An ex-clergyman has fallen into a state of confusion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in disarray' rearranges PRIEST and IN; the first 'in' is part of that phrase, the second is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Pristine can mean belonging to the earliest period, in an original state, hence earlier or of old.

clue.text: Fuss follows fellows following football

indicators.note: fellows following football means their letters are placed after it

parts.note: FA is the Football Association
F is short for fellow, doubled for the plural like pp for pages

explanation.surface: A row breaks out after some men follow football.
explanation.walkthrough: 'follows' is only a link; 'following' sets the order. FAFF is British slang for time-wasting fuss, as in faffing about.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for needless fuss or dithering, as in faffing about.

clue.text: Only place to store documents one by one

definitions.meaning: read literally: just one folder to keep papers in
in a line, each person behind another

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means walking in a line, one behind another, and also playfully describes papers all kept in one folder.

clue.text: Doffs one's cap, then loses it

definitions.meaning: literally raises or tips the top of the head off, a lid being slang for a hat

explanation.definitionFit: Lid is slang for a hat, so tipping one's hat is the literal sense, while the idiom means to fly into a rage.

clue.text: Investigation about home-counties' principal

parts.note: re means about or concerning
the Home Counties around London lie in the South East, SE
arch means chief or principal, as in arch-enemy

explanation.surface: An inquiry concerns the leading figure of the area around London.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the English counties around London, in the South East.
explanation.definitionFit: Systematic study to establish facts, a synonym for inquiry or investigation.

clue.text: Tried by former foreign secretary, they say

indicators.note: they say signals that the word is what people hear spoken, not how it is spelt

parts.note: Douglas Hurd was British Foreign Secretary from 1989 to 1995

explanation.surface: A case was judged by an ex-government minister, according to reports.
explanation.walkthrough: Douglas Hurd was a British Foreign Secretary; his surname sounds like the answer. 'Tried' is in the court sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A court case that has been listened to and judged has been tried before a judge.

clue.text: Way to get money? Baloney!

parts.note: a drive is a road or way, as in street names
L stands for the pound, from Latin libra, British money

explanation.surface: Someone asks how to earn cash, and gets told it is nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get' links the pieces. L is the pound sign's letter, for the British pound sterling.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean nonsense or rubbish talk, silly empty chatter.

clue.text: Old seamen take responsibility

parts.note: NUS was the National Union of Seamen, a British trade union

explanation.surface: Veteran sailors shoulder the duty.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Union of Seamen (NUS) was a British trade union for merchant sailors.
explanation.definitionFit: A burden or duty that falls on someone, as in the burden of proof.

clue.text: Ploy Vera used to get ham

indicators.note: used in the sense of worked over or exploited, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman named Vera uses a trick to land some pork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used' rearranges PLOY and VERA. 'ham' looks like meat but is the verb for over-acting.
explanation.definitionFit: To ham is to act in an exaggerated way, laying it on too thick on stage.

clue.text: Long for king Charles to accept greeting

parts.note: CR is Carolus Rex, the royal cipher of King Charles
ave is Latin for hail, a greeting

explanation.surface: A subject yearns for the monarch to acknowledge a salute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to accept' links the pieces, CR taking AVE after it. CR stands for Carolus Rex, Latin for King Charles.
explanation.definitionFit: To desire intensely, to yearn or hanker after something.

clue.text: Many a French friend has only an undergarment

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so many
ami is French for friend
sole means only, as in the sole survivor

explanation.surface: Lots of men's French pals own nothing but their underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' and 'an' are links between the pieces and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A light sleeveless top worn under clothes, a woman's underwear item.

clue.text: Peter is not at risk

definitions.meaning: old criminal slang for a strongbox, which safecrackers call a peter

explanation.definitionFit: Peter is underworld slang for a strongbox, and the adjective means out of danger.

clue.text: Fortress on secure headland

parts.note: fast means firmly fixed, as in hold fast
a ness is a promontory, as in Loch Ness's neighbours and place names

explanation.surface: A castle stands on a well-protected promontory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' joins the pieces in a down clue. NESS appears in British place names for a cape or promontory.
explanation.definitionFit: A stronghold or secure retreat, a place well fortified against attack.

clue.text: In Trieste employees are treated with respect

indicators.note: in means the letters sit inside the words Trieste employees, running across them

explanation.surface: Workers in an Italian port city are handled with courtesy.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'TriESTE EMployees'; 'are treated with' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: High regard or admiration felt for someone, a synonym for respect.

clue.text: Make less food with little content

indicators.note: content as contents: the small word is held inside the food word

parts.note: a dish is a plate of food
mini means small or little

explanation.surface: A tiny portion of food is served to reduce a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content' is read as contents, what the food holds; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To reduce or lessen in size or amount.

clue.text: Way to acquire sound property

indicators.note: sound signals that the property word is heard spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: a manor is a landed estate, a property

explanation.surface: A method for buying a solid piece of real estate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like an adjective meaning solid; it signals the homophone. 'to acquire' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Manner means a way or method of doing something.

clue.text: Spurn tigress resolved to take financial control

indicators.note: resolved read as re-solved, broken up and put together afresh, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A determined female tiger spurns someone to seize the money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resolved' rearranges SPURN and TIGRESS; 'to take' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Whoever holds these cords of a money bag controls the spending of a household or organisation.

clue.text: Enthralled by artillery exercises

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery
PT is physical training, exercises

explanation.surface: A spectator is gripped by gunnery drills.
explanation.walkthrough: RA is the Royal Artillery, a British army regiment; PT is physical training.
explanation.definitionFit: Completely absorbed or fascinated, held spellbound.

clue.text: Rex takes snake out of grating

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for rex, Latin for king
an asp is a venomous snake

explanation.surface: A king takes a serpent out of a drain cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grating' suggests a metal grille, but is the adjective for a harsh scraping sound; 'out of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A harsh, scraping noise or voice, as rough and abrasive as a coarse file.

clue.text: Song that told a story

definitions.meaning: a German art song, as by Schubert

explanation.definitionFit: A German art song for voice and piano, and the past tense of fibbing.

clue.text: They carry injections for a thousand French hens

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
poules is French for hens

explanation.surface: A poultry farmer pays a thousand for French hens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link between definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Small sealed glass vials holding a single dose of drug for a syringe.

clue.text: Island in march is bliss

indicators.note: in places the island abbreviation inside the march word

parts.note: a parade is a march past

explanation.surface: A procession on an island is pure joy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'march' is a procession, not the month; 'is' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A state of perfect happiness, heaven on earth.
